open_points.subject: A17 configuration and credential path placement
open_points.text: These paths lie outside the kernel's private directory
open_points.question: Is placement outside the kernel's private directory a required, checked condition, or merely an explanation of the threat, since no rule refuses a configuration or secret path inside that directory?
options: Refuse any configuration or credential path inside the private directory
Allow paths anywhere if the ownership, mode and symlink checks pass
Require outside placement operationally but do not verify it
open_points.default_guess: Treat the sentence as explanatory and allow any path that passes the stated checks.

open_points.subject: A18 failed store call after encountering a symbolic link
open_points.text: a link met so later makes that store call fail with nothing written
open_points.question: Does "nothing written" prohibit every filesystem artifact, or only durable records, given rule 3 says a failed call may leave a published file that no record names?
options: No database record changes, but an unreferenced published file may remain
No record or file may be written or published by the call
Writes completed before the link was encountered may remain
open_points.default_guess: Allow only the already-specified unreferenced published file while rolling back all records.

open_points.subject: A18 opening the data directory itself
open_points.text: opened relative to the data directory it holds open from the start
open_points.question: How must the data-directory path itself be opened, and are symbolic links in that path or its ancestor components refused?
options: Open every component without following symbolic links, as in A17
Follow ancestor links but require the final object to be a private directory
Allow the final data-directory path itself to be a symbolic link and hold its target open
open_points.default_guess: Open the data-directory path component by component without following symbolic links and reject any link.

open_points.subject: A18 filesystem operations other than open
open_points.text: Every file the store opens itself is opened relative to the data directory it holds open from the start, each component with Linux's `O_NOFOLLOW`
open_points.question: What happens when a symbolic link is encountered as the destination or operand of rename, unlink, stat, directory scanning or cleanup rather than by opening a file?
options: Any store filesystem operation that encounters a link fails the store call
Only opens are protected; other operations may replace or remove a link without following it
Operations may proceed whenever they do not dereference the link
open_points.default_guess: Detect the link without following it and fail the store call for every store filesystem operation.

open_points.subject: A20 supported Linux environment
open_points.text: A release runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named
open_points.question: Which Linux kernel and filesystem capabilities are required for `O_PATH`, component-wise `O_NOFOLLOW`, namespaces, limits and bubblewrap, and what exact behavior applies on a Linux host lacking one of them?
options: Support every Linux host on which the release can start
State a minimum Linux/kernel capability set
Probe required capabilities at startup and refuse to start when any is unavailable
open_points.default_guess: Probe the required operations at startup and refuse to start with a bounded reason when one is unavailable.
